issue.title: Report table shows Chilean peso amounts a thousand times too small
issue.body:
Our Santiago office's account is in CLP. In the report table, a payment of
$12.500 from the bank file shows as CLP 13, and $8.990 shows as CLP 9. I think
`src/components/ReportTable.tsx` formats pesos as if they had cents and divides
somewhere along the way; the bank file itself is correct. The CSV export of the
same report says 13 and 9 as well. Last month's file, which had one transfer of
-$1.250.000, was rejected with 'The amount is not a number' at that row.

input.title: Parse dot-grouped zero-decimal amounts (CLP) correctly in parseAmount
input.body:
File: src/util/money.ts

parseAmount only strips commas as thousands separators and treats "." as the decimal point. For zero-decimal currencies such as CLP, "12.500" is read as 12.5 and rounded to 13, and "-1.250.000" fails the /^\d+(\.\d+)?$/ check and returns null (hence 'The amount is not a number'). Change parseAmount so that, when minorDigits(currency) is 0, "." (and ",") are treated as grouping separators and removed before validation, so "12.500" becomes 12500 and "-1.250.000" becomes -1250000. The report table and CSV export only display the stored value, so they need no change.

The problem is in parseAmount, not in ReportTable.tsx. It treats "." as the decimal point and only strips commas. For CLP, which has no minor unit, "12.500" is read as 12.5 and rounded to 13. The account's 312 imported CLP rows were all stored with this rounding. "-1.250.000" has two dots, so it fails the number check and raises errors.badAmount. The table and CSV only display the stored value, so they show the wrong numbers. I opened a draft PR (pr-2) that treats separators as grouping for zero-decimal currencies.
